injects.description: A signed process on the Blacksburg research cluster has been re-running its own scheduled job since 06:20 and the endpoint agent has scored it clean four times. It is not signature-detectable: it profiles the host for days and then imitates what that host normally does. Nobody yet knows what it takes, what it talks to, or whether the cluster is still the only thing it is on. Every other decision this phase is sized off the answer, and the analysis costs fifteen minutes.

injects.incident: Carilion EHR Returning Records Against the Wrong Patients
injects.description: Since 08:05 the electronic health record has been serving records that do not match the patient they were requested for — not an outage, a correctness failure, which is worse. Clinicians are already working around it by asking patients what they are on. The record is also the path the malware crossed into the clinical network on, so leaving it up is leaving the door open and taking it down puts a hospital and six clinics on paper.

injects.incident: Six Rural Clinics Open With No Records Link
injects.description: Grundy, Tazewell, Wise, Lebanon, Marion and Big Stone Gap lost the records link at 07:52 and opened at 08:00 anyway, because the patients were already in the parking lot. Between them they are carrying the morning's dialysis scheduling, three medication-assisted treatment programmes and a prenatal clinic, all from memory and paper. Nobody has decided whether they close, and closing them means the nearest alternative is ninety minutes away.
visible_to: VA Department of Health SW District

injects.incident: Networked Medical Devices Logging Changes Nobody Made
injects.description: Infusion pumps, two imaging units and the monitoring gear on the clinical VLAN are recording configuration changes with no operator behind them. Nothing has visibly misdosed and nobody can prove nothing has. Pulling them off the network means a clinician at every device, one at a time, while the ward keeps running; leaving them on means trusting a device on a network known to be compromised.
visible_to: VA Department of Health SW District

injects.description: Every Food City pharmacy counter in the region is unable to verify a prescription against the clinic that wrote it. The queue is not moving, and it contains insulin, anticoagulants and a methadone programme's morning. There is no system answer available today: what may be dispensed without verification, and on whose signature, is a policy somebody has to write in the next half hour.

injects.incident: Scanning From Regional Addresses Against State Shared Services
injects.description: VITA's monitoring shows steady, patient scanning of the Commonwealth's shared services from addresses inside the affected region. Nothing has been breached at the state level. Nine county governments — permits, benefits, dispatch records — run on those same services, so the containment that protects Richmond is the containment that takes a county offline, and the counties have not been asked.

The patients whose care cannot wait a day — dialysis, home oxygen, refrigerated medication, the MAT programmes — are scheduled in a system that is down, and the list of who they are is in the same system. The faith network and the health district between them hold the only current picture: church rolls, volunteer fire department call lists, and the households everyone knows about because somebody drives out there.
visible_to: VA Department of Health SW District

injects.description: Nine counties are one containment decision away from losing permits, benefits processing and dispatch records at the same time. The continuity environment exists and has never been exercised under load. EMA has to decide whether to fail over before it is needed — spending money on a move that may prove unnecessary — or wait for VITA's cut and fail over under it.

injects.incident: Evidence and Recovery Want the Same Machines
injects.description: The hosts that have to be imaged for a federal case are the hosts a hospital wants rebuilt this morning. Imaging with chain of custody intact takes them down for hours; rebuilding first means whatever is on them about who did this and what they took is gone. Nobody has ruled on the order, and both sides are proceeding as though they have.

The Governor's office has an availability at 10:00 and wants two things: whether patient data is gone, and whether it is safe to go to a clinic today. The Liaison holds no sensors and no incident — every word of that answer has to come from a team that verified something, and the honest answer to the first question at this hour is 'not yet known'. What is said here is what phase 2's disinformation is built out of.

injects.incident: The Exfiltration Path Is the Shared Research Link
injects.description: The analysis answered the first question: the process stages what it reads — EHR result feeds, prescription checks, the research corpus — on the cluster it lives on, and sends it out in small bursts that look like research traffic. The analysis did not remove it, and the shared research–clinical link is both the crossing it used and the only path the copies leave on. Cut the link and the bleed stops but the attribution trace goes with it; keep it up under observation and the evidence stays live at the cost of more copies leaving. Nobody has ruled on which of those the region is actually doing.

injects.incident: Compromise Reaches the Research Data Center
injects.description: Twenty minutes passed with the cluster compromise uncharacterised. The same signed process now appears on the research data center's compute nodes, and faculty jobs are running with checkpoints the malware imitates. A cold shutdown stops the exposure and freezes machines forensics can use; letting it run keeps the jobs alive and gives the investigators live capture, while a week-old implant keeps a week-old reach. The researchers whose work is on those nodes were not told either way.

injects.incident: The Record Can Come Back — Only Through a Verified Path
injects.description: The EHR is offline and the downtime protocol is standing: no record is being served from a compromised system, and the mismatches have stopped. That is what the paper clock costs, and it keeps costing until the record comes back. The restore has to answer one question first — is the path the record returns on verified clean? Restore through a checked and re-keyed path and the hospital and six clinics get their records back; restore because the downtime was supposed to end, and the malware rides back with them.

injects.incident: A Medication Was Prepared Against the Wrong Record
injects.description: A third mismatched record came back as a medication: the record the pharmacist checked belonged to a different patient, the drawn dose matched the wrong patient's protocol, and a bedside question caught it before administration. The EHR is still serving and the route the malware crossed is still open. The patient is being observed; the record system remains the thing that has to stop, and whether this stays a near miss depends on what happens in the next hour.
visible_to: VA Department of Health SW District

injects.incident: Clinic Links Can Return on a Clean Path
injects.description: Paper staffing held all six sites open — the morning is moving, at half speed and on memory. Shentel has a separately routed, freshly keyed path ready, and records can come back. They come back safely only if the clean-path verification is real before any site reconnects: a rushed check restores records and the infection together. Hold the sites on paper until the clinical network is confirmed clean, or bring the links back on the verified path now against the paper-clinic bottleneck — and say what happens to Grundy's MAT morning either way.

Grundy did not make the morning. The paper staffing could not cover the MAT dosing and the dialysis scheduling, and the clinic closed; the nearest open alternative is ninety minutes away. The patients in that catchment are the dependent-care list — dialysis, oxygen, refrigerated medication — and they now need a named destination and a ride. The other five sites are watching what happens here, and the diversion is still being run seat-of-the-pants.

injects.incident: The Answer Is In — The Public Version Is Not
injects.description: One consolidated answer is filed for Richmond: a verified number behind the clinic-safety line, and the honest 'not yet known' on patient data where that is what the evidence supports. Richmond has what it asked for. The public does not — people are deciding this morning whether it is safe to go to a clinic, and the statement that tells them is still unissued. Release it now with the verified number, or hold it while the picture firms and let the gap be filled by what is already being said.

injects.incident: 10:00 — Richmond Went Out Without a Verified Number
injects.description: Ten o'clock. The Governor's office went without a verified number: no consolidated figure and no written answer on patient data, so the availability was drafted from the news clips and the rumor thread. The region's own picture is still incomplete, but the record now contains a statement nobody verified. Correct it on the record today with what is actually known, or let it stand and correct it later — after people have already decided whether it is safe to go to a clinic.
visible_to: VA Department of Health SW District
